props.gloss_en: one who sees a place where miracles were done for Israel says: Blessed... who did miracles for our fathers in this place
a place from which idolatry was uprooted, he says: Blessed... who uprooted idolatry from our land
over zikin, zeva'ot, thunder, winds and lightning he says: Blessed... whose strength and might fill the world
over mountains, hills, seas, rivers and deserts he says: Blessed... who makes creation
R' Yehuda: one who sees the great sea says: Blessed... who made the great sea
R' Yehuda: when he sees it at intervals
over rain and good tidings he says: Blessed... the good and who does good
over bad tidings he says: Blessed... the true Judge
one who built a new house or bought new vessels says: Blessed... who has kept us alive, sustained us and brought us to this time
one blesses over the bad in the manner of [blessing] over the good, and over the good in the manner of [blessing] over the bad
one who cries out over the past -- this is a vain prayer
his wife was pregnant and he says 'may it be [Your] will that my wife bear a male' -- this is a vain prayer
he was coming on the road, heard a cry in the city and says 'may it be [Your] will that it not be in my house' -- this is a vain prayer
one who enters a city prays two [prayers], one on entering and one on leaving
Ben Azzai: four, two on entering and two on leaving
he gives thanks for the past and cries out for the future
a person is obligated to bless over the bad as he blesses over the good
as it is said: 'and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart...' (Deut 6:5)
'with all your heart' -- with your two inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination
'and with all your soul' -- even if He takes your soul
'and with all your might' -- with all your money
another interpretation: 'with all your might' -- for whatever measure He metes out to you, give thanks to Him
a person may not act lightly opposite the eastern gate
for it is aligned opposite the Holy of Holies
and he may not enter the Temple Mount with his staff, his shoes, his money belt, or the dust on his feet
and he may not make it a shortcut
and spitting [is forbidden there] a fortiori
all who closed blessings in the Temple used to say 'until the world'
they enacted that one say 'from the world to the world'
[this was enacted] when the heretics corrupted and said there is but one world
and they enacted that a person greet his fellow with the Name
as it is said: 'and behold Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, the Lord be with you; and they said to him, the Lord bless you' (Ruth 2:4)
and it says: 'the Lord is with you, mighty man of valour' (Judg 6:12)
and it says: 'and do not despise [her] when your mother is old' (Prov 23:22)
and it says: 'it is a time to act for the Lord; they have voided Your Torah' (Ps 119:126)
R' Natan: 'they have voided Your Torah' -- because 'it is a time to act for the Lord'

schemas.gloss_en: ורקיקה מקל וחומר -- if entering with one's staff, shoes, money belt or dusty feet is forbidden on the Temple Mount, spitting there is forbidden all the more
